data.narrative:
Deep Fission, founded by Liz Muller and Rich Muller, is a nuclear energy company preparing for IPO after raising $80M in total capital. The valuation universe comprises 9 nuclear energy peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 6 private firms including X-Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this analysis. The nuclear energy sector contains only one company at Deep Fission's IPO stage, with zero additional peers at adjacent stages or comparable valuation tiers. A minimum of three comparable datapoints is required for reliable peer-median analysis. Restricting the comp set to narrow stage and tier filters eliminates the possibility of meaningful triangulation via this method; expanding to all six nuclear energy peers would introduce substantial stage and business model heterogeneity and would not reflect Deep Fission's specific positioning.

Without sufficient near-stage peers to establish a defensible multiple range, quantitative valuation cannot be reliably triangulated from the available data. Deep Fission's IPO pricing will depend heavily on underwriter roadshow feedback, public market appetite for nuclear energy equities at the time of offering, and company-specific metrics not captured in this peer universe. The primary uncertainty is the absence of IPO-stage nuclear comparables, limiting the precision of forward valuation estimates.
